audit_status.source_base: Greek Titus text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for civic posture, kindness and renewal, heirs, good works, foolish disputes, divisive person, final greetings.

verses.restored: Remind them to be arranged under rulers and authorities, to obey, to be ready for every beautiful/good work,

familiar.text: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work,

modern.text: Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient and ready for every good work,

original.text: Ὑπομίμνῃσκε αὐτοὺς ⸀ἀρχαῖς ἐξουσίαις ὑποτάσσεσθαι πειθαρχεῖν, πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἑτοίμους εἶναι,

verses.restored: to blaspheme/slander no one, to be non-quarrelsome, gentle, showing all meekness toward all humans.

familiar.text: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.

modern.text: to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.

original.text: μηδένα βλασφημεῖν, ἀμάχους εἶναι, ἐπιεικεῖς, πᾶσαν ἐνδεικνυμένους πραΰτητα πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους.

verses.restored: For we also were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, passing life in harmfulness and envy, hated and hating one another.

familiar.text: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

modern.text: For at one time we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, and enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures—living in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.

original.text: ἦμεν γάρ ποτε καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀνόητοι, ἀπειθεῖς, πλανώμενοι, δουλεύοντες ἐπιθυμίαις καὶ ἡδοναῖς ποικίλαις, ἐν κακίᾳ καὶ φθόνῳ διάγοντες, στυγητοί, μισοῦντες ἀλλήλους.

verses.restored: But when the kindness and love-for-humanity of our Savior/Healer Divine appeared,

familiar.text: But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,

modern.text: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared,

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἡ χρηστότης καὶ ἡ φιλανθρωπία ἐπεφάνη τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ,

verses.restored: not from works in righteousness/justice that we did, but according to his mercy, he saved/healed us through washing of rebirth and renewal of holy Spirit,

familiar.text: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;

modern.text: He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

original.text: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων τῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ⸀ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς ἀλλὰ κατὰ ⸂τὸ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος⸃ ἔσωσεν ἡμᾶς διὰ λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας καὶ ἀνακαινώσεως πνεύματος ἁγίου,

verses.restored: which he poured out upon us richly through Jesus Messiah our Savior/Healer,

familiar.text: Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;

modern.text: This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

original.text: οὗ ἐξέχεεν ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς πλουσίως διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν,

verses.restored: so that, having been made righteous/just by his grace, we might become heirs according to hope of age-long life.

familiar.text: That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

modern.text: so that, having been justified by His grace, we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life.

original.text: ἵνα δικαιωθέντες τῇ ἐκείνου χάριτι κληρονόμοι ⸀γενηθῶμεν κατʼ ἐλπίδα ζωῆς αἰωνίου.

verses.restored: Trustworthy is the saying; and concerning these things I desire you to insist, so that those having trusted the Divine may be careful to stand before beautiful/good works. These things are beautiful/good and beneficial to humans.

familiar.text: This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

modern.text: This saying is trustworthy. And I want you to emphasize these things, so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are excellent and profitable for the people. Avoid Divisions (Romans 16:17–20)

original.text: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος, καὶ περὶ τούτων βούλομαί σε διαβεβαιοῦσθαι, ἵνα φροντίζωσιν καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι οἱ πεπιστευκότες θεῷ. ταῦτά ⸀ἐστιν καλὰ καὶ ὠφέλιμα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·

verses.restored: But avoid foolish inquiries and genealogies and strifes and fights about Law, for they are unbeneficial and empty.

familiar.text: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

modern.text: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.

original.text: μωρὰς δὲ ζητήσεις καὶ γενεαλογίας καὶ ⸀ἔρεις καὶ μάχας νομικὰς περιΐστασο, εἰσὶν γὰρ ἀνωφελεῖς καὶ μάταιοι.

verses.restored: A divisive human, after one and a second admonition, refuse,

familiar.text: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;

modern.text: Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition,

original.text: αἱρετικὸν ἄνθρωπον μετὰ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν νουθεσίαν παραιτοῦ,

verses.restored: knowing that such a one has been turned out of alignment and is sinning/missing the mark, being self-condemned.

familiar.text: Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.

modern.text: knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned. Final Remarks and Greetings

original.text: εἰδὼς ὅτι ἐξέστραπται ὁ τοιοῦτος καὶ ἁμαρτάνει, ὢν αὐτοκατάκριτος.

verses.restored: When I send Artemas to you or Tychicus, be eager to come to me at Nicopolis, for there I have decided to winter.

familiar.text: When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.

modern.text: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.

original.text: Ὅταν πέμψω Ἀρτεμᾶν πρὸς σὲ ἢ Τυχικόν, σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με εἰς Νικόπολιν, ἐκεῖ γὰρ κέκρικα παραχειμάσαι.

verses.restored: Diligently send forward Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that nothing may be lacking to them.

familiar.text: Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.

modern.text: Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.

original.text: Ζηνᾶν τὸν νομικὸν καὶ ⸀Ἀπολλῶν σπουδαίως πρόπεμψον, ἵνα μηδὲν αὐτοῖς λείπῃ.

verses.restored: And let our people also learn to stand before beautiful/good works for necessary needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.

familiar.text: And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.

modern.text: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.

original.text: μανθανέτωσαν δὲ καὶ οἱ ἡμέτεροι καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι εἰς τὰς ἀναγκαίας χρείας, ἵνα μὴ ὦσιν ἄκαρποι.

verses.restored: All those with me greet you. Greet those loving us in trust. Grace be with all of you.

familiar.text: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.

modern.text: All who are with me send you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with all of you.

original.text: Ἀσπάζονταί σε οἱ μετʼ ἐμοῦ πάντες. ἄσπασαι τοὺς φιλοῦντας ἡμᾶς ἐν πίστει. ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων ⸀ὑμῶν.

translation_notes: Civic submission language must be bounded by good works, gentleness, and non-slander; it is not absolute obedience to injustice.
Regeneration/renewal is mercy and Spirit language, not self-achievement.
Good works are repeatedly framed as beneficial, necessary, and fruitful.
